data.narrative:
Aclarity is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Julie Bliss Mullen, having raised $14M to date. The valuation landscape includes one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers spanning the sector, including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, no narrow peer set of same-stage or adjacent-stage companies with similar valuation tiers yielded sufficient datapoints for reliable median-based triangulation.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable approach here. Using total capital raised ($14M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $28M. This represents the central estimate given the absence of robust peer-median data within the Climate & Energy sector at comparable stages.

The analysis supports a range of $24M to $32M, with a median estimate of $28M. This relatively narrow band reflects reliance on a single methodological pillar. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficiently sized peer comparable sets at Aclarity's stage within the sector—a constraint that limits cross-validation—and the inherent sensitivity of stage-progression methods to assumed step-up multipliers. Any material deviation from 2.0x progression would materially shift the implied valuation.
